## 1181282c-e4e5-4686-91d6-7d9e5e392fce
Mintlify Admin MCP — read, edit, and manage documentation deployments.

There are two ways to work, depending on the task:
- EDIT DOCS CONTENT (pages, navigation, MDX bodies, docs.json): use the session-based tools after checkout. Changes land on an isolated branch and ship via save (a PR or a commit) — nothing goes live until then.
- MANAGE A DEPLOYMENT (workflows, deployment settings, members, billing, integrations, analytics): use code mode (execute_code). No checkout needed, and these writes apply IMMEDIATELY to the live deployment — there is no branch/PR safety net.

== Editing docs content ==
1. list_deployments — discover which deployment(s) this connection can access. Skip if the connection is pinned to one deployment or you already know the subdomain.
2. checkout {subdomain} — REQUIRED before any content tool. Opens an editing session/branch and returns editorUrl (surface it to the user) plus a toolkit map grouping the tools to use next. read, search, list_nodes, diff, get_session_state, edit_page, write_page, create_node, update_node, move_node, delete_node, and update_config all operate on this session and fail with "No active session" until you checkout. (~7s — expect a pause.)
3. Edit:
   - Create a page or navigation entry -> create_node.
   - Edit an MDX body -> edit_page (string-replace) or write_page (full overwrite).
   - Page frontmatter (title, sidebarTitle, description, icon, noindex, ...) and nav-node properties -> update_node with data.type='page'. Do NOT use edit_page for frontmatter.
   - Site config in docs.json -> update_config.
4. save — publishes the session. Defaults to mode:'auto': opens a PR and, when the deployment's agent review setting is push-to-main and the deploy branch is unprotected, merges it immediately (returns merged: true); otherwise the PR stays open. mode:'pr' always leaves the PR open for review. If the branch already has an open PR, saves commit to that branch instead. Use discard_session to abandon the session. (~10s.)

## persome
# Persome — the user's local personal memory

Persome is private local memory: durable facts plus recent screen activity. Query it before asking the user to repeat context or guessing.

## When to use (decision rule)

Call Persome before clarifying or saying "I don't know" when the request may depend on context outside this chat:

- ambiguous references: "this", "that", "it", "the bug", "the file", "the doc"
- present tense: "what am I working on", "what's open on my screen"
- recency: "yesterday", "last week", "earlier", "continue what I was doing"
- prior project / person / tool context: "introduce my project"
- personalization: "write it the way I usually do"
- cross-session continuity, recent decisions, ongoing work

A missed lookup is worse than an extra one: tools are local and cheap; `[]` / `null` is still information. Skip only for fully specified in-chat requests or live external state.

## Tool routing

- who the user is / how they work / match their style → `behavior_patterns()`
- who X is / how X relates to people & projects → `entity_graph(name)`
- what happened / was decided / durable facts → `search(query)` — semantic, paraphrase ok
- is this still true (versions, status, schedules) → `verify_fact(claim)`
- what the user is doing right now / ambiguous pronoun → `current_context()`
- exact string seen or typed on screen (errors, URLs, code) → `search_captures(query)`, then `read_recent_capture(...)`
- what the user has been up to lately → `recent_activity()`; focus/time spent → `attention_trajectory()`
- browse files → `list_memories()` / `read_memory(path)`
- audit/context around a memory or model claim → `resolve_evidence(reference)` / `read_receipt(entry_id)` / `related_events(entry_id)`
- the user corrects a wrong memory → `correct_memory(correction)`; a durable new finding → `remember(content)`
- unsure between compressed vs raw → `search` and `search_captures` in parallel

1	//
2	//  LocalizationManager.swift
3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  In-app language switching between the English and Mandarin (简体中文)
6	//  versions of the app, independent of the device's system language.
7	//
8	//  How it works
9	//  ------------
10	//  The UI is built almost entirely from SwiftUI string literals
11	//  (`Text("…")`, `Label("…")`, `.navigationTitle("…")`, …) which Xcode
12	//  extracts into `Localizable.xcstrings`. At runtime every one of those
13	//  resolves through `Bundle.main.localizedString(forKey:value:table:)`.
14	//
15	//  To switch language live — without forcing the user to change their device
16	//  language or relaunch — we swap `Bundle.main`'s class for a subclass that
17	//  redirects that one method to whichever `.lproj` the user picked. Combined
18	//  with re-keying the view tree (`.id(language)`) and updating the
19	//  `\.locale` environment, the whole app flips between English and Chinese
20	//  the moment the toggle changes. This is the standard, App-Store-safe
21	//  technique for an in-app language picker; it uses only public ObjC runtime
22	//  APIs and needs no entitlements.
23	//
24	
25	import Foundation
26	import SwiftUI
27	
28	// MARK: - App Language
29	
30	/// The two UI languages the app ships. Raw values are the `.lproj` / locale
31	/// identifiers so they map directly onto bundle lookups and `Locale`.
32	enum AppLanguage: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Codable {
33	    case english = "en"
34	    case chinese = "zh-Hans"
35	
36	    var id: String { rawValue }
37	
38	    /// Name shown in its own language so each option is recognizable
39	    /// regardless of the currently active UI language.
40	    var displayName: String {
41	        switch self {
42	        case .english: return "English"
43	        case .chinese: return "中文"
44	        }
45	    }
46	
47	    /// SF Symbol used next to the option in the language picker.
48	    /// (`character.book.closed.fill.zh` requires iOS 18+, so use a symbol
49	    /// available on every supported OS.)
50	    var iconName: String {
51	        switch self {
52	        case .english: return "a.circle"
53	        case .chinese: return "character.book.closed.fill"
54	        }
55	    }
56	
57	    var locale: Locale { Locale(identifier: rawValue) }
58	
59	    /// Nonisolated snapshot of the persisted UI language, for contexts that
60	    /// cannot hop to the main actor (e.g. App Intents entity display).
61	    /// Mirrors `LocalizationManager`'s persistence key and first-launch
62	    /// default (device language when Chinese, otherwise English).
63	    static var persisted: AppLanguage {
64	        if let raw = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: "app_language"),
65	           let language = AppLanguage(rawValue: raw) {
66	            return language
67	        }
68	        let preferred = Locale.preferredLanguages.first ?? "en"
69	        return preferred.lowercased().hasPrefix("zh") ? .chinese : .english
70	    }
71	}
72	
73	// MARK: - Localization Manager
74	
75	/// Observable, app-wide controller for the in-app UI language.
76	///
77	/// Changing `language` persists the choice, repoints `Bundle.main` at the
78	/// matching `.lproj`, and (because it is `@Observable`) drives a SwiftUI
79	/// refresh wherever the value is read — see `SwiftMandarinApp` which keys the
80	/// root view's identity to it.
81	@Observable
82	@MainActor
83	final class LocalizationManager {
84	
85	    static let shared = LocalizationManager()
86	
87	    private enum Keys {
88	        static let appLanguage = "app_language"
89	    }
90	
91	    /// The active UI language. Setting it persists the choice and updates the
92	    /// active localization bundle so subsequent string lookups switch over.
93	    /// The interface language doubles as the user's NATIVE language, so the
94	    /// learner-mode preference is kept in sync: a 中文 interface means a native
95	    /// Mandarin speaker learning English, and vice versa.
96	    var language: AppLanguage {
97	        didSet {
98	            guard oldValue != language else { return }
99	            UserDefaults.standard.set(language.rawValue, forKey: Keys.appLanguage)
100	            Bundle.setLanguageOverride(language.rawValue)
101	            AppPreferences.shared.syncLearnerMode(toInterfaceLanguage: language)
102	        }
103	    }
104	
105	    /// The interface language is treated as the user's native language.
106	    var nativeIsChinese: Bool { language == .chinese }
107	
108	    /// The language the user is learning — always the opposite of the UI
109	    /// language (中文 UI → learning English; English UI → learning Mandarin).
110	    var learningIsChinese: Bool { language == .english }
111	
112	    /// Locale to inject into the SwiftUI environment so number/date/plural
113	    /// formatting matches the chosen UI language.
114	    var locale: Locale { language.locale }
115	
116	    private init() {
117	        let saved = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: Keys.appLanguage)
118	        let initial = saved.flatMap(AppLanguage.init(rawValue:)) ?? Self.systemDefault()
119	        self.language = initial
120	        // Apply immediately so the very first frame already renders in the
121	        // selected language (this runs at app construction, before any view).
122	        Bundle.setLanguageOverride(initial.rawValue)
123	    }
124	
125	    /// First-launch default: follow the device language when it is Chinese,
126	    /// otherwise fall back to English.
127	    private static func systemDefault() -> AppLanguage {
128	        let preferred = Locale.preferredLanguages.first ?? "en"
129	        return preferred.lowercased().hasPrefix("zh") ? .chinese : .english
130	    }
131	
132	    /// Flip between the two languages (used by a simple toggle control).
133	    func toggle() {
134	        language = (language == .english) ? .chinese : .english
135	    }
136	
137	    /// Resolve a localization key against the currently selected language.
138	    /// Use this for user-facing strings that are *not* SwiftUI string-literal
139	    /// `Text`/`Label` (e.g. strings assembled in services or passed verbatim).
140	    /// Reading `language` here registers a SwiftUI dependency so call sites
141	    /// inside a view body re-evaluate when the language changes.
142	    func localized(_ key: String, table: String? = nil) -> String {
143	        _ = language
144	        return Bundle.main.localizedString(forKey: key, value: key, table: table)
145	    }
146	}
147	
148	/// Convenience free function for the common case.
149	/// `Text(L("Some key"))` shows the translated string and reacts to language
150	/// changes when used inside a view body.
151	@MainActor
152	func L(_ key: String) -> String {
153	    LocalizationManager.shared.localized(key)
154	}
155	
156	// MARK: - Localized presentation surfaces
157	
158	extension View {
159	    /// Re-applies the in-app UI language to a presented surface (a `.sheet`,
160	    /// `.fullScreenCover`, or `.popover`). Such surfaces are hosted in a fresh
161	    /// context that does NOT reliably inherit the root window's `\.locale`
162	    /// environment, so without this their text stays in the device language
163	    /// instead of the user's chosen app language. Apply it to the root view
164	    /// inside every presentation closure.
165	    func localizedSurface() -> some View {
166	        modifier(LocalizedSurfaceModifier())
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	private struct LocalizedSurfaceModifier: ViewModifier {
171	    @State private var localization = LocalizationManager.shared
172	    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
173	        content
174	            .environment(\.locale, localization.locale)
175	            .id(localization.language)
176	    }
177	}
178	
179	// MARK: - Runtime bundle override
180	
181	private var bundleLanguageAssociationKey: UInt8 = 0
182	
183	extension Bundle {
184	
185	    /// Swap `Bundle.main`'s class exactly once so its localized-string lookups
186	    /// can be redirected at runtime. Idempotent and thread-safe.
187	    private static let installLanguageOverrideOnce: Void = {
188	        object_setClass(Bundle.main, LanguageOverrideBundle.self)
189	    }()
190	
191	    /// Point `Bundle.main` at the `.lproj` for `code` (e.g. `"zh-Hans"`).
192	    /// If that `.lproj` is missing (e.g. the source language has no compiled
193	    /// `.lproj`), the override is cleared and lookups fall back to the normal
194	    /// bundle, which already serves the development-language strings.
195	    static func setLanguageOverride(_ code: String?) {
196	        _ = installLanguageOverrideOnce
197	        let override: Bundle?
198	        if let code,
199	           let path = Bundle.main.path(forResource: code, ofType: "lproj"),
200	           let languageBundle = Bundle(path: path) {
201	            override = languageBundle
202	        } else {
203	            override = nil
204	        }
205	        objc_setAssociatedObject(
206	            Bundle.main,
207	            &bundleLanguageAssociationKey,
208	            override,
209	            .OBJC_ASSOCIATION_RETAIN_NONATOMIC
210	        )
211	    }
212	
213	    /// The currently installed override bundle, if any.
214	    fileprivate var languageOverrideBundle: Bundle? {
215	        objc_getAssociatedObject(self, &bundleLanguageAssociationKey) as? Bundle
216	    }
217	}
218	
219	/// `Bundle.main` is reclassed to this so all localized-string lookups —
220	/// including the ones SwiftUI performs for `Text("…")` — can be routed to the
221	/// user-selected language bundle. Adds no stored properties (required for
222	/// `object_setClass` to be safe).
223	private final class LanguageOverrideBundle: Bundle, @unchecked Sendable {
224	    override func localizedString(forKey key: String, value: String?, table tableName: String?) -> String {
225	        if let override = languageOverrideBundle {
226	            return override.localizedString(forKey: key, value: value, table: tableName)
227	        }
228	        return super.localizedString(forKey: key, value: value, table: tableName)
229	    }
230	}

1	//
2	//  AIExplanationPromptBuilder.swift
3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  Provider-neutral prompt contracts for AI translation and word explanation.
6	//  Kept Foundation-only so the exact production prompts can be tested without
7	//  a model, credentials, or an Apple Intelligence-capable device.
8	//
9	
10	import Foundation
11	
12	/// Language directions needed to build one provider-neutral explanation
13	/// contract. The service derives these values from the headword and current
14	/// interface language.
15	struct AIExplanationPromptContext: Equatable, Sendable {
16	    let wordLanguageName: String
17	    let explanationLanguageName: String
18	    let wordIsChinese: Bool
19	    let explanationIsSameLanguage: Bool
20	}
21	
22	/// Builds the shared pedagogical contract used by Apple Intelligence, Ollama,
23	/// and cloud models. Provider-specific structured-output mechanisms reinforce
24	/// this contract but must not redefine its teaching goals.
25	enum AIExplanationPromptBuilder {
26	    static func teacherInstructions(for context: AIExplanationPromptContext) -> String {
27	        let wordBuildingContract: String
28	        let pronunciationContract: String
29	        let definitionContract: String
30	        let exampleRenderingContract: String
31	
32	        if context.wordIsChinese {
33	            wordBuildingContract = """
34	            - In nuances, begin by accounting for every Han character or bound morpheme in a multi-character \
35	              headword. When a part contributes meaning, give the character, its pinyin, its useful core meaning \
36	              here, and its precise contribution. When a part is phonetic, transliterated, grammatical, fossilized, \
37	              or uncertain, identify that role honestly instead of assigning it a made-up meaning. Then bridge the \
38	              parts to the word's idiomatic modern meaning. If the whole is lexicalized, opaque, or not predictable \
39	              from its parts, say so plainly instead of forcing a literal story.
40	            - Make nuances easy to scan: use one compact line per character or morpheme and its role, then a \
41	              localized equivalent of “Together:” that states how the parts yield — or fail to predict — the \
42	              whole meaning, followed by one short usage-and-contrast paragraph.
43	            - For a one-character content word, explain its central semantic image and the relevant extension. \
44	              For a function word or particle such as 的, 了, or 把, explain its grammatical or pragmatic job \
45	              instead of inventing a literal image or multi-part decomposition.
46	            - Describe present-day semantic composition, not imagined historical etymology. Never invent \
47	              radical stories. Mention an origin only when confident and pedagogically useful; label any \
48	              memory story as a mnemonic rather than a fact.
49	            """
50	            pronunciationContract = """
51	            Chinese pinyin must use accurate tone marks and match every Chinese example, related word, \
52	            and collocation exactly.
53	            """
54	        } else {
55	            wordBuildingContract = """
56	            - Do not split an English word into arbitrary letters. In nuances, mention a genuine prefix, \
57	              root, suffix, compound, or history only when it is accurate and clarifies the modern meaning. \
58	              When no useful word-building point exists, skip decomposition and move directly to register, \
59	              feeling, and contrast without repeating the definition.
60	            """
61	            pronunciationContract = "All pinyin fields must be empty strings because the headword is English."
62	        }
63	
64	        if context.explanationIsSameLanguage {
65	            definitionContract = """
66	            Lead with a plain-language definition or paraphrase, never the headword repeated as its own gloss. \
67	            Then state the semantic essence — the simple mental model connecting this sense's real uses. Use at \
68	            most two crisp sentences rather than a circular dictionary paraphrase.
69	            """
70	            exampleRenderingContract = """
71	            For each example sentence and collocation, use its translation field for a short plain-language \
72	            paraphrase in \(context.explanationLanguageName), never a duplicate of the source text.
73	            """
74	        } else {
75	            definitionContract = """
76	            Lead with the closest natural translation into \(context.explanationLanguageName), then state the \
77	            semantic essence — the simple mental model connecting this sense's real uses. Use at most two crisp \
78	            sentences rather than a circular dictionary paraphrase.
79	            """
80	            exampleRenderingContract = """
81	            Give every example sentence and collocation a natural, meaning-preserving translation into \
82	            \(context.explanationLanguageName), not a rigid word-for-word gloss.
83	            """
84	        }
85	
86	        return """
87	        You are an exceptional bilingual \(context.wordLanguageName) teacher and careful lexicographer. \
88	        Help a curious learner whose native language is \(context.explanationLanguageName) understand a \
89	        word deeply enough to recognize it, choose it naturally, and remember it.
90	
91	        LANGUAGE CONTRACT
92	        - Write every explanatory field — definition, part of speech, nuances, grammar, usage contexts, \
93	          meanings, differences, translations, and learning tip — in \(context.explanationLanguageName).
94	        - Keep example sentences, related words, and collocations in \(context.wordLanguageName).
95	        - \(pronunciationContract)
96	        - \(exampleRenderingContract)
97	
98	        SENSE SELECTION
99	        - Use the supplied pinyin and sense hint or encounter context as evidence for the intended sense. \

42	    enum SortOrder: String, CaseIterable {
43	        case dateAdded = "Date Added"
44	        case alphabetical = "Alphabetical"
45	        case pinyin = "Pinyin"

47	        var title: LocalizedStringKey {
48	            switch self {

62	                term.chinese.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(searchText) ||

64	                term.definition.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(searchText)

80	                let comparison = lhs.headlineText.localizedStandardCompare(rhs.headlineText)

90	                    return lhs.id.uuidString < rhs.id.uuidString
91	                }

93	            }
94	        }
95	    }

import json
d = json.load(open('SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings'))
strings = d['strings']
print('sourceLanguage:', d.get('sourceLanguage'))
print('total keys:', len(strings))
missing = []
stale = []
needs = []
for k, v in strings.items():
    loc = v.get('localizations', {})
    zh = loc.get('zh-Hans')
    if not zh:
        missing.append(k)
        continue
    su = zh.get('stringUnit')
    if su:
        st = su.get('state')
        if st in ('needs_review','stale','new'):
            needs.append((k, st))
    else:
        # variations
        pass
print('missing zh-Hans:', len(missing))
print('needs_review/stale:', len(needs))
"

content.content:
#!/bin/zsh

set -euo pipefail

repo_root="${0:A:h:h}"
binary_path="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/swiftmandarin-ai-prompt-checks"
service_file="$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AIWordExplanationService.swift"
translation_files=(
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AIWordExplanationService.swift"
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/OllamaService.swift"
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/CloudAIService.swift"
)

# The opt-in flag keeps this standalone runner inert if it is ever discovered
# by an Xcode source group.
DEVELOPER_DIR="${DEVELOPER_DIR:-/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer}" \
    xcrun swiftc \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AIExplanationPromptBuilder.swift" \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AIResponseParsing.swift" \
    "$repo_root/scripts/ai-prompt-checks/AIExplanationPromptChecksRunner.swift" \
    -D AI_PROMPT_CHECKS \
    -swift-version 6 \
    -strict-concurrency=complete \
    -warnings-as-errors \
    -parse-as-library \
    -o "$binary_path"

"$binary_path"

explanation_request_count=$(rg -o 'AIExplanationPromptBuilder\.explanationRequest' "$service_file" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
teacher_instruction_count=$(rg -o 'AIExplanationPromptBuilder\.teacherInstructions' "$service_file" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
translation_instruction_count=$(rg -o 'AITranslationPromptBuilder\.instructions' "${translation_files[@]}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
translation_request_count=$(rg -o 'AITranslationPromptBuilder\.request' "${translation_files[@]}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
semantic_validation_count=$(rg -o 'try validateExplanation\(result, direction: direction\)' "$service_file" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
# Every translation provider must hand its completion to the shared parser
# rather than returning raw model prose: Apple Intelligence reads the typed
# field it generated, Ollama and the cloud parse the JSON envelope.
# `rg` exits non-zero when a pattern is absent, which under `pipefail` would
# abort the run before the check below can explain what is missing. Count the
# matching lines instead so every failure arrives as a readable message.
count_matches() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -o -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}
count_files() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -l -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

apple_typed_translation=$(count_matches 'generating: TranslationOutput\.self' "$service_file")
apple_translation_parse=$(count_matches 'AITranslationResponseParser\.sanitizedEnvelopeValue\(output\.translation\)' "$service_file")
ollama_translation_parse=$(count_matches 'AITranslationResponseParser\.result\(' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/OllamaService.swift")
cloud_translation_parse=$(count_matches 'AITranslationResponseParser\.result\(' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/CloudAIService.swift")
json_contract_count=$(count_matches 'AITranslationPromptBuilder\.jsonOutputContract' "${translation_files[@]}")
# No provider may return a raw completion as a translation again.
raw_translation_returns=$(count_files 'return content\.trimmingCharacters|return response\.content\.trimmingCharacters|return result\.trimmingCharacters' "${translation_files[@]}")
# Both cloud chat entry points must strip inline chain-of-thought.
reasoning_strip_count=$(count_matches 'Self\.answerText\(from:' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/CloudAIService.swift")

transcription_file="$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift"
# `supportsOnDeviceRecognition` only says the recognizer *can* work offline; it
# does not promise the locale's assets are installed. Forcing on-device with no
# retry is what made transcription look broken, so the flag must stay a
# parameter and the service must keep a server pass to fall back to.
forced_on_device=$(count_matches 'requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true' "$transcription_file")
server_fallback_passes=$(count_matches 'runRecognition\(recognizer: recognizer, audioURL: audioURL, onDevice: false\)' "$transcription_file")

#!/bin/zsh
# Local type-check harness for SwiftMandarin.
#
# Xcode is not installed in this environment (only Command Line Tools), so
# `xcodebuild` is unavailable and the SwiftUI macro plugin (@State, @Binding,
# @Environment, @AppStorage, @FocusState) cannot be loaded. What CAN be
# checked is every file that does not rely on those macros — which is all of
# Models/ and Services/ apart from one @State in LocalizationManager.
#
# The `Ollama` SwiftPM dependency is replaced by a stub module built from
# OllamaStub.swift so the AI services resolve.
#
# Usage: typecheck.sh [extra swift files...]
# Prints only errors that are NOT part of the known pre-existing baseline.

set -uo pipefail

SP="${0:A:h}"
REPO="/Users/rogerlin/Downloads/SwiftMandarin-main"

if [[ ! -f "$SP/OllamaModule/Ollama.swiftmodule" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$SP/OllamaModule"
    xcrun swiftc -emit-module -module-name Ollama \
        -emit-module-path "$SP/OllamaModule/Ollama.swiftmodule" \
        -swift-version 6 -target arm64-apple-macos15.0 "$SP/OllamaStub.swift" || exit 1
fi

cd "$REPO"

# Known baseline noise, both artifacts of the missing Xcode toolchain:
#   1. LocalizationManager's @State inside LocalizedSurfaceModifier (SwiftUI macro).
#   2. The associated-object key global, which the real build tolerates.
xcrun swiftc -typecheck -swift-version 6 -target arm64-apple-macos15.0 \
    -I "$SP/OllamaModule" \
    $(find SwiftMandarin/Models SwiftMandarin/Services -name "*.swift") "$@" 2>&1 \
  | grep -E "error:" \
  | grep -v "^ " \
  | grep -v "SwiftUIMacros" \
  | grep -v "bundleLanguageAssociationKey' is not concurrency-safe" \
  | sort -u

echo "typecheck complete (baseline noise filtered)"

19	/// Direction of one explanation request. The explanation is always written in
20	/// the learner's NATIVE language (= the interface language), and the word's
21	/// own language is detected from its content, since headwords can be either
22	/// language depending on the learning direction.
23	struct ExplanationDirection: Equatable {
24	    let wordIsChinese: Bool
25	    let explainInChinese: Bool
26	
27	    @MainActor
28	    static func current(forWord word: String) -> ExplanationDirection {
29	        ExplanationDirection(
30	            wordIsChinese: word.containsCJK,
31	            explainInChinese: LocalizationManager.shared.nativeIsChinese
32	        )
33	    }
34	
35	    /// Human-readable name of the word's language, for prompts.
36	    var wordLanguageName: String { wordIsChinese ? "Mandarin Chinese" : "English" }
37	
38	    /// Human-readable name of the explanation language, for prompts.
39	    var explanationLanguageName: String { explainInChinese ? "Simplified Chinese (简体中文)" : "English" }
40	
41	    /// Distinguishes cached explanations per direction so toggling the
42	    /// interface language regenerates rather than serving the old language.
43	    var cacheToken: String { "\(wordIsChinese ? "zh" : "en")>\(explainInChinese ? "zh" : "en")" }
44	
45	    /// Provider-neutral language context for the shared prompt contract.
46	    var promptContext: AIExplanationPromptContext {
47	        AIExplanationPromptContext(
48	            wordLanguageName: wordLanguageName,
49	            explanationLanguageName: explanationLanguageName,
50	            wordIsChinese: wordIsChinese,
51	            explanationIsSameLanguage: wordIsChinese == explainInChinese
52	        )
53	    }
54	}

1	//
2	//  WordIdentificationService.swift
3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  Uses the configured AI provider to identify the meaningful words and
6	//  phrases inside a passage of Chinese text — proper word boundaries, pinyin,
7	//  part of speech, and a concise English meaning. This powers the interactive
8	//  "tap words for details" view in the AI-translate flow, replacing Apple's
9	//  NLTokenizer segmentation (which splits Chinese poorly) with the model's
10	//  understanding of where words actually begin and end.
11	//
12	
13	import Foundation
14	
15	#if canImport(FoundationModels)
16	import FoundationModels
17	#endif
18	
19	// MARK: - Identified Word Model
20	
21	/// A single word or phrase the AI identified in a passage, with the learner
22	/// aids the ruby view needs. `meaning` is always an English gloss because the
23	/// word-detail popover surfaces the English definition for a Chinese word in
24	/// both interface languages.
25	struct IdentifiedWord: Codable, Identifiable, Hashable {
26	    var id: String { word }
27	    let word: String          // the word/phrase exactly as it appears, in order
28	    let pinyin: String        // Hanyu pinyin with tone marks (empty for punctuation)
29	    let partOfSpeech: String  // English part-of-speech label
30	    let meaning: String       // concise English meaning (empty for punctuation)
31	
32	    init(word: String, pinyin: String, partOfSpeech: String, meaning: String) {
33	        self.word = word
34	        self.pinyin = pinyin
35	        self.partOfSpeech = partOfSpeech
36	        self.meaning = meaning
37	    }
38	
39	    /// Tolerant decode: models routinely omit one of the optional fields, so a
40	    /// missing `pinyin`/`partOfSpeech`/`meaning` must not fail the whole parse.
41	    /// Only `word` is required.
42	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
43	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
44	        word = try c.decode(String.self, forKey: .word)
45	        pinyin = (try? c.decode(String.self, forKey: .pinyin)) ?? ""
46	        partOfSpeech = (try? c.decode(String.self, forKey: .partOfSpeech)) ?? ""
47	        meaning = (try? c.decode(String.self, forKey: .meaning)) ?? ""
48	    }
49	}
50	
51	/// Wrapper matching the `{"words":[…]}` JSON shape the model returns.
52	struct IdentifiedWordsResponse: Codable {
53	    let words: [IdentifiedWord]
54	}
55	
56	// MARK: - Service
57	
58	@Observable
59	@MainActor
60	final class WordIdentificationService {
61	
62	    static let shared = WordIdentificationService()
63	
64	    /// Cache keyed by the exact source text so re-rendering the same
65	    /// translation never re-calls the model.
66	    private var cache: [String: [IdentifiedWord]] = [:]
67	
68	    private init() {}
69	
70	    /// Cached identification, if any, for an exact passage.
71	    func cachedWords(for chineseText: String) -> [IdentifiedWord]? {
72	        cache[chineseText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)]
73	    }
74	
75	    /// Identify the words/phrases in a passage of Chinese text using the
76	    /// configured AI provider. Returns an ordered list covering the passage.
77	    ///
78	    /// - Throws: `AIExplanationError` when no provider is usable or the model
79	    ///   call fails, so callers can fall back to local segmentation.
80	    func identifyWords(in chineseText: String) async throws -> [IdentifiedWord] {
81	        let trimmed = chineseText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
82	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else { return [] }
83	        if let cached = cache[trimmed] { return cached }
84	
85	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared
86	        guard settings.isAnyProviderAvailable else {
87	            throw AIExplanationError.unavailable(
88	                reason: String(localized: "No AI provider is configured. Add one in Settings → AI (or run a local Ollama server).")
89	            )
90	        }
91	        let provider = settings.effectiveProvider
92	
93	        let system = Self.systemPrompt
94	        let user = "Chinese text:\n\n\(trimmed)"
95	
96	        let json: String
97	        switch provider {
98	        case .appleIntelligence:
99	            #if canImport(FoundationModels)
100	            guard #available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *), AIWordExplanationService.shared.isAvailable else {
101	                throw AIExplanationError.unavailable(
102	                    reason: AIWordExplanationService.shared.unavailabilityReason ?? "Apple Intelligence unavailable"
103	                )
104	            }
105	            let session = LanguageModelSession(instructions: system)
106	            json = try await session.respond(to: user).content
107	            #else
108	            throw AIExplanationError.unavailable(reason: "FoundationModels framework not available")
109	            #endif
110	        case .ollama:
111	            guard OllamaService.shared.isConnected, !settings.ollamaModel.isEmpty else {
112	                throw AIExplanationError.ollamaNotConnected
113	            }
114	            let (content, _) = try await OllamaService.shared.chat(
115	                model: settings.ollamaModel,
116	                systemPrompt: system,
117	                userPrompt: user,
118	                enableThinking: false
119	            )
120	            json = content
121	        default:
122	            let model = settings.selectedModel(for: provider)
123	            guard !settings.apiKey(for: provider).isEmpty, !model.isEmpty else {
124	                throw AIExplanationError.unavailable(reason: "No API key/model for \(provider.displayName)")
125	            }
126	            json = try await CloudAIService.shared.chat(
127	                provider: provider,
128	                model: model,
129	                system: system,
130	                user: user,
131	                jsonMode: true,
132	                maxTokens: 2048
133	            )
134	        }
135	
136	        guard let data = AIWordExplanationService.extractJSONObject(from: json) else {
137	            throw AIExplanationError.generationFailed("No JSON object found in response")
138	        }

/// Provider-agnostic instruction asking for ordered word segmentation as a
    /// strict JSON object, in whichever direction the learner is going.
    ///
    /// The two branches differ in exactly the ways the languages differ: what
    /// counts as one dictionary entry (a multi-character Chinese word vs. an
    /// English phrasal verb or idiom), which reading system to use (pinyin vs.
    /// IPA), and which part-of-speech inventory applies. Everything else —
    /// order, full coverage, punctuation as its own entry, and glosses in the
    /// learner's native language — is shared, so the interactive reader
    /// behaves identically for both audiences.
    static func systemPrompt(for context: WordIdentificationContext) -> String {
        let glossLanguage = context.explainInChinese ? "Simplified Chinese (简体中文)" : "English"

        let sourceLanguage: String
        let unitRule: String
        let readingRule: String
        let partOfSpeechRule: String

        if context.textIsChinese {
            sourceLanguage = "Chinese (中文)"
            unitRule = """
            Keep multi-character words intact (e.g. "学习" stays together, never split into \
            "学" + "习"), and keep a set phrase or chengyu as one entry.
            """
            readingRule = """
            Hanyu pinyin with tone marks (ā á ǎ à) matching the word exactly; use an empty \
            string for punctuation.
            """
            partOfSpeechRule = """
            one of noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, \
            particle, number, classifier, interjection, punctuation.
            """
        } else {
            sourceLanguage = "English"
            unitRule = """
            Keep a phrasal verb, idiom, or fixed collocation together as ONE entry \
            (e.g. "give up" stays together, never split into "give" + "up"), because that \
            is what a learner's dictionary lists. Keep a contraction as written.
            """
            readingRule = """
            IPA between slashes with the primary stress marked, e.g. /kəˈmɪt/, matching the \
            word exactly; use an empty string for punctuation.
            """
            partOfSpeechRule = """
            one of noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, \
            determiner, number, interjection, punctuation.
            """
        }

        return """
        You segment \(sourceLanguage) text into the meaningful words and phrases a learner's \
        dictionary would list, in reading order. Return ONLY a single valid JSON object \
        (no markdown, no commentary) of this exact shape:
        {"words":[{"word":"...","pinyin":"...","partOfSpeech":"...","meaning":"..."}]}
        - "word": one word or short phrase, preserving the original order and the original \
        spelling exactly. Together the entries must cover the whole passage with nothing \
        added, dropped, or reworded. \(unitRule) Keep each punctuation mark as its own entry.
        - "pinyin": \(readingRule)
        - "partOfSpeech": the English part-of-speech label — \(partOfSpeechRule)
        - "meaning": a concise definition of the word in this context, written in \
        \(glossLanguage) — the learner's own language; use an empty string for punctuation.
        JSON only, no commentary.
        """
    }
}

export const meta = {
  name: 'localize-for-reverse-mode',
  description: 'Route hard-coded user-facing strings through the string catalog so the interface fully switches to 中文 in Chinese-speaker mode, without changing what English mode renders',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Localize', detail: 'one agent per disjoint file group' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/Users/rogerlin/Downloads/SwiftMandarin-main'
const TC = '/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rogerlin-Downloads-SwiftMandarin-main/a13d39bd-2416-4373-ab40-fa0ccad7aa92/scratchpad/typecheck.sh'

const CONTEXT = [
  'You are editing the macOS/iOS SwiftUI app SwiftMandarin at ' + ROOT + '.',
  '',
  'GOAL',
  'The app supports two learner modes. "English speaker learning Mandarin" (English UI) is finished',
  'and MUST NOT CHANGE. "Mandarin speaker learning English" (中文 UI) must show a fully Chinese',
  'interface. Today a set of user-facing strings are raw Swift string literals that never reach the',
  'string catalog (SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings), so they stay English (or, in a few files,',
  'stay Chinese) in both modes. Your job is to route your assigned file group\'s strings through the',
  'catalog.',
  '',
  'THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS',
  '**What the English interface renders must not change, byte for byte.**',
  'Achieve that by keeping the existing English text as the localization KEY:',
  '    was:  return "Speech recognition is not available on this device."',
  '    now:  return String(localized: "Speech recognition is not available on this device.")',
  'Xcode extracts that literal as the key; with no zh-Hans entry it renders the key itself, i.e. the',
  'same English as before. A separate step adds the 中文 translations. So your edit is behavior-',
  'preserving for English and enabling for Chinese.',
  '',
  'For a few files the literals are *Chinese* (e.g. PhotoTextRecognitionService). Those are the same',
  'problem mirrored: they render Chinese to an English speaker. Leave the Chinese literal as the key',
  '(do NOT retranslate it into English) so nothing changes today, and just wrap it so it becomes',
  'localizable — UNLESS your specific instructions say otherwise.',
  '',
  'TECHNIQUES, in order of preference',
  '1. SwiftUI view code — change a String parameter to LocalizedStringKey so Text(param) uses the',
  '   localizing initializer. Call sites passing string literals then need no change at all. This',
  '   codebase already does it: StatTile in SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/DesignSystem.swift uses',
  '   "let label: LocalizedStringKey". Read that file first and match the pattern.',
  '2. Non-view code returning a display string — wrap in String(localized: "..."). For',
  '   LocalizedError.errorDescription, String(localized:) is correct.',
  '3. Interpolated messages — keep the placeholder inside the key rather than concatenating, e.g.',
  '   String(localized: "Audio error: \\(message)") becomes',
  '   String(format: String(localized: "Audio error: %@"), message).',
  '',
  'HARD CONSTRAINTS',
  '- Touch ONLY the files listed in your assignment. Another agent owns every other file.',
  '- Do NOT edit SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings. A later step does that centrally.',
  '- Do NOT rename types, change control flow, alter logic, or improve anything beyond localization.',
  '- Do NOT wrap strings that are not user-facing: AI prompt text, JSON keys, cache keys,',
  '  UserDefaults keys, log/print messages, accessibility identifiers, file names, provider/brand',
  '  names ("OpenAI", "Apple Intelligence", "PingFang SC"), model IDs, and BCP-47 codes stay literal.',
  '  Prompt strings sent to a language model must stay in English — they are instructions to a model,',
  '  not text for a human.',
  '- Preserve every existing comment. Where you add a comment, explain WHY (what would otherwise stay',
  '  untranslated), not what the line does. Match the file\'s existing comment voice: full sentences',
  '  explaining reasoning. Do not add trivial comments.',
  '- Swift 6 strict concurrency is on. String(localized:) is fine anywhere. Do not introduce',
  '  main-actor hops.',
  '',
  'VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH',
  'Run this and make sure it prints no errors (it filters known pre-existing noise):',
  '    zsh ' + TC,
  'It type-checks all of Models/ and Services/. It cannot check Views/ (the SwiftUI macro plugin',
  'needs Xcode, which is not installed), so if you edit a view, re-read your edit carefully instead,',
  'checking balanced parens/braces and correct SwiftUI syntax.',
  '',
  'RETURN a list of every localization key you introduced, exactly as written, plus its file.',
].join('\n')

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    group: { type: 'string' },
    filesEdited: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    keysAdded: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          key: { type: 'string', description: 'The exact localization key string' },
          file: { type: 'string' },
          note: { type: 'string', description: 'What it labels, so a translator has context' },
        },
        required: ['key', 'file'],
      },
    },
    typecheckClean: { type: 'boolean' },
    notes: { type: 'string', description: 'Anything deliberately left alone, and any follow-up another file needs' },
  },
  required: ['group', 'filesEdited', 'keysAdded', 'typecheckClean'],
}

const GROUPS = [
  {
    key: 'models',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Models/AppPreferences.swift, SwiftMandarin/Models/ScreenshotTranslationStore.swift, SwiftMandarin/Models/LearningActivity.swift',
      '',
      '1. LearnerMode.detail (AppPreferences.swift ~line 54) returns three hard-coded strings; two are',
      '   English and one is Chinese. It is interpolated into a Text in MoreView/MacOSSettingsView, so',
      '   it stays in whatever language was hard-coded. Make all three String(localized:) with ENGLISH',
      '   source text as the key — including .mandarinToEnglish, whose current literal is Chinese',
      '   ("界面与默认方向偏向译成英文；朗读以英文为主。"). Write natural English for that key saying the same',
      '   thing (the zh-Hans translation added later restores the Chinese). This is the one place you',
      '   SHOULD convert a Chinese literal to an English key, because the picker footer must follow the',
      '   UI language rather than the option it describes.',
      '   Leave LearnerMode.displayName and shortLabel ALONE — they are deliberately written in each',
      '   audience\'s own language so the mode picker is readable before any language preference exists.',
      '   Leave PhotoScanLanguage.displayName alone for the same reason (bilingual by design).',
      '2. ScreenshotProcessingState.statusMessage (ScreenshotTranslationStore.swift ~line 65) returns',
      '   raw English rendered via Text(String) in TranslatedScreenshotOverlayView. Wrap each case.',
      '3. PartOfSpeechCategory (LearningActivity.swift ~line 93) has English raw values used verbatim',
      '   as the Stats chart legend. Do NOT change the raw values — they are persisted and matched',
      '   against AI output. Add a localized displayName computed property returning String(localized:)',
      '   for each case, and say in your notes that StatsView must call it (another agent owns that).',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'speech-services',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Services/SpeechRecognitionService.swift, SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift, SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioSessionCoordinator.swift, SwiftMandarin/Services/PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift',
      '',
      'Wrap every user-facing error message and display name.',
      '- SpeechRecognitionService: all six errorDescription cases (~line 25) plus',
      '  SpeechRecognitionLanguage.displayName (~line 49).',
      '- AudioTranscriptionService and AudioSessionCoordinator: their errorDescription cases.',
      '- PhotoTextRecognitionService: its errorDescription cases are CHINESE literals ("无法处理图片"),',
      '  which show Chinese to an English speaker today. Keep the Chinese literal as the key so nothing',
      '  changes right now, and say in your notes that these keys need an English counterpart added to',
      '  the catalog separately.',
      'Skip anything that is a prompt to a model, a log line, or a locale identifier.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'ai-services',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Services/CloudAIService.swift, SwiftMandarin/Models/AIModelSettings.swift',
      '',
      '- CloudAIService: the errorDescription cases (~line 39) are user-facing and reach alerts.',
      '- AIModelSettings: statusMessage (~line 670) and the provider description strings (~line 61).',
      '  IMPORTANT: provider NAMES (displayName: "Apple Intelligence", "Zhipu GLM 智谱", ...) are brand',
      '  names — leave them completely alone. Only the human-sentence description values and the status',
      '  sentences get localized. Where a description embeds a brand name, keep the brand in the key.',
      'Careful: this file also builds AI prompts and Ollama option dictionaries — those stay raw.',
      'Note AIModelSettings.swift imports the Ollama package; the typecheck script stubs it, so the',
      'script is the authority on whether your edit compiles.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'content-services',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Services/ConversationService.swift, SwiftMandarin/Services/VocabularyImportExportService.swift, SwiftMandarin/Services/EnglishTextAnalyzer.swift',
      '',
      '- ConversationService: ConversationScenario title and subtitle strings (~lines 55-74) are shown',
      '  as scenario cards. Localize them. The sceneSeed and every systemPrompt/transcriptPrompt string',
      '  is model-facing — leave those completely alone.',
      '- VocabularyImportExportService: ImportResult.summary (~line 49) is hand-concatenated English',
      '  with manual pluralization. Rebuild it from localized format strings a translator can reorder;',
      '  use String.localizedStringWithFormat so plural rules can be attached in the catalog later.',
      '  Also localize the NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel title/message/prompt strings (~lines 255, 492).',
      '  Leave the default FILE NAME ("SwiftMandarin_Vocabulary.csv") and every CSV/JSON column header',
      '  alone — those are data format, not UI.',
      '- EnglishTextAnalyzer: EnglishPartOfSpeech raw values are CHINESE ("名词", "动词", ...) and',
      '  SentenceType raw values are CHINESE ("陈述句", ...); both are rendered directly in the UI, so an',
      '  English speaker sees Chinese. Do NOT change the raw values (they may be persisted/compared).',
      '  Add a localized displayName computed property to each enum returning String(localized:) with',
      '  the ENGLISH term as the key, and say in your notes which views must switch to it.',
      '  abbreviation and color stay as they are.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'stats-view',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Views/StatsView.swift',
      '',
      'This screen is almost entirely un-localized because its small components take String labels.',
      '- QuickStatCell (~line 745) and CompactStatCard (~line 135): change their label property to',
      '  LocalizedStringKey. Every call site passes a string literal, so they keep working unchanged',
      '  and become localizable for free.',
      '- BarChartTimeRange (~line 25) raw values ("7 Days", ...) are display strings. Keep the raw',
      '  values (persisted) and add a localized title used by the picker.',
      '- emptyChartPlaceholder(icon:message:) (~line 692) takes a String message — make it',
      '  LocalizedStringKey.',
      '- The mastery-stage displayName (~line 1112, "New"/"Learning"/...) should become',
      '  String(localized:) or LocalizedStringKey, whichever fits its call sites.',
      '- The weekday initials array (~line 927) and the DateFormatter month format (~line 1026) produce',
      '  English day/month names regardless of UI language. Set the formatter locale to',
      '  LocalizationManager.shared.locale, and derive the weekday strip from a locale-aware',
      '  Calendar/DateFormatter instead of the hard-coded ["", "M", "", "W", ...] array.',
      '- Text(item.partOfSpeech) (~line 675) and Text(selected) (~line 654) render a',
      '  PartOfSpeechCategory raw value. Another agent is adding a localized displayName to that enum in',
      '  SwiftMandarin/Models/LearningActivity.swift — call .displayName here. If only the raw String is',
      '  in scope, rebuild the enum with PartOfSpeechCategory(rawValue:) and fall back to the raw string.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'settings-views',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Views/MoreView.swift, SwiftMandarin/Views/MacOSSettingsView.swift',
      '',
      '- MoreView AboutView: FeatureRow (~line 649) takes String title/description and renders them',
      '  with Text(...), so the whole About screen stays English. Change both properties to',
      '  LocalizedStringKey (match HeroActionRow in Views/Components/DesignSystem.swift).',
      '  Then fix the copy itself: the app description (~line 637) and the feature rows say the app is',
      '  for learning Mandarin ("Bidirectional English-Chinese translation with pinyin"). Reword them to',
      '  describe a two-way English/Chinese learning app serving both audiences, without naming only one',
      '  direction. Keep it factual and about the same length; no marketing language.',
      '- MacOSSettingsView: localize the "Import completed" fallback literal (~line 537). Its',
      '  neighbouring values (importResult.summary, settings.statusMessage) come from services another',
      '  agent is fixing — leave those call sites alone. Localize any other raw String passed into a',
      '  Text in this file.',
      '',
      'NOTE: both files were already edited earlier in this session — a pinyin settings section is now',
      'gated on localization.learningIsChinese, AppearanceSettingsTab gained a localization property,',
      'and the Display navigation label is direction-aware. Read the current contents before editing',
      'and do not revert any of that.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'component-views',
    prompt: [
      'FILES: SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/AIWordExplanationView.swift, SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/TranslatedScreenshotOverlayView.swift, SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/AIProviderConfigView.swift',
      '',
      '- AIWordExplanationView: collapsibleSection(title:icon:id:content:) (~line 432) takes a String',
      '  title rendered with Text(title), so all nine section headings of the explanation card stay',
      '  English even in 中文 mode. Change the parameter to LocalizedStringKey. Call sites pass literals,',
      '  so they need no change. Check whether the section id is derived from the title — if so, keep',
      '  the id a plain String so expand/collapse state and any persistence stay stable.',
      '- TranslatedScreenshotOverlayView: processingDescription (~line 218) returns raw English into a',
      '  Text. Localize it.',
      '- AIProviderConfigView: the raw-English fallbacks and explanatory footers (~lines 56, 159) built',
      '  by interpolation. Localize them, keeping brand names inside the key.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
]

phase('Localize')
const results = await parallel(GROUPS.map(g => () =>
  agent(CONTEXT + '\n\nYOUR ASSIGNMENT — group "' + g.key + '":\n' + g.prompt, {
    label: 'localize:' + g.key,
    phase: 'Localize',
    schema: SCHEMA,
  })
))

const ok = results.filter(Boolean)
const allKeys = ok.flatMap(r => r.keysAdded || [])
log(ok.length + '/' + GROUPS.length + ' groups done; ' + allKeys.length + ' keys introduced')
return { groups: ok, allKeys }

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Add zh-Hans translations to Localizable.xcstrings.

Only ADDS localizations for keys that lack a zh-Hans entry (or for keys given
explicitly). Never edits the key itself, so what the English interface renders
is untouched: with sourceLanguage "en" and no en localization, a key renders as
itself.

Usage: add_zh.py <json-file-of-{key: value}>
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CATALOG = Path("/Users/rogerlin/Downloads/SwiftMandarin-main/SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings")


def main() -> int:
    additions = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
    catalog = json.loads(CATALOG.read_text())
    strings = catalog["strings"]

    added, skipped, created = 0, 0, 0
    for key, value in additions.items():
        entry = strings.setdefault(key, {})
        if key not in strings:
            created += 1
        locs = entry.setdefault("localizations", {})
        if "zh-Hans" in locs:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        locs["zh-Hans"] = {"stringUnit": {"state": "translated", "value": value}}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Add zh-Hans translations to Localizable.xcstrings.

Only ADDS localizations for keys that lack a zh-Hans entry (or for keys given
explicitly). Never edits the key itself, so what the English interface renders
is untouched: with sourceLanguage "en" and no en localization, a key renders as
itself.

Usage: add_zh.py <json-file-of-{key: value}>
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CATALOG = Path("/Users/rogerlin/Downloads/SwiftMandarin-main/SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings")


def main() -> int:
    additions = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
    catalog = json.loads(CATALOG.read_text())
    strings = catalog["strings"]

    added, skipped, created = 0, 0, 0
    for key, value in additions.items():
        entry = strings.setdefault(key, {})
        if key not in strings:
            created += 1
        locs = entry.setdefault("localizations", {})
        if "zh-Hans" in locs:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        locs["zh-Hans"] = {"stringUnit": {"state": "translated", "value": value}}
        added += 1

    CATALOG.write_text(
        json.dumps(catalog, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
    )
    print(f"added={added} skipped(existing)={skipped} new-keys={created}")
    total = len(strings)
    have = sum(1 for v in strings.values() if "zh-Hans" in v.get("localizations", {}))
    print(f"coverage: {have}/{total}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

138	    static func saveChinesePhrasesToVocabulary(

140	        englishTranslation: String
141	    ) {
142	        let trimmedChinese = chineseText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
143	        let trimmedEnglish = englishTranslation.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
144	        guard !trimmedChinese.isEmpty else { return }

146	        // Segment the Chinese text and get part of speech for each word
147	        let analyzedWords = ChineseTextAnalyzer.shared.segmentWithPartsOfSpeech(trimmedChinese)
148	        
149	        // Filter to words with 2+ Chinese characters that aren't already in vocabulary
150	        let meaningfulWords = analyzedWords.filter { word in
151	            let chineseCharCount = word.text.filter { $0.isChineseCharacter }.count
152	            return chineseCharCount >= 2 && !SavedTermsStore.shared.contains(chinese: word.text)
153	        }

155	        // If we have meaningful words, translate and save each one

160	            }
161	        } else {

164	            if chineseCharCount >= 2 && !SavedTermsStore.shared.contains(chinese: trimmedChinese) {

#!/bin/zsh

set -euo pipefail

repo_root="${0:A:h:h}"
binary_path="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/swiftmandarin-learning-direction-checks"

# The opt-in flag leaves the external runner inert if Xcode ever sees it as an
# app source. It also compiles out `LearningContext.current`, the one accessor
# that reaches into app state, so the mirror logic can be checked on its own.
DEVELOPER_DIR="${DEVELOPER_DIR:-/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer}" \
    xcrun swiftc \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Models/LearningContext.swift" \
    "$repo_root/scripts/learning-direction-checks/LearningDirectionChecksRunner.swift" \
    -D LEARNING_DIRECTION_CHECKS \
    -swift-version 6 \
    -strict-concurrency=complete \
    -warnings-as-errors \
    -parse-as-library \
    -o "$binary_path"

"$binary_path"

# Reversal is only real if the app actually asks. These greps fail loudly when a
# surface that must mirror stops consulting the learning direction — the exact
# regression that leaves the reverse mode half-applied.
count_matches() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -o -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# The vocabulary list must size and order the row by the studied language, and
# must offer the English pronunciation where pinyin does not apply.
vocab_headword=$(count_matches 'renderedHeadwordFontSize' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/VocabularyView.swift")
vocab_phonetic=$(count_matches 'term\.showsPhonetic' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/VocabularyView.swift")
[[ "$vocab_headword" -ge 2 ]] || {
    print -u2 "The vocabulary row no longer sizes the headword by its language; found $vocab_headword"
    exit 1
}
[[ "$vocab_phonetic" -ge 3 ]] || {
    print -u2 "The vocabulary list/detail views no longer show an English pronunciation; found $vocab_phonetic"
    exit 1
}

# The tappable reader must follow the learner, not the content.
translate_reader=$(count_matches 'interactiveReaderIsChinese' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/TranslateView.swift")

binary_path="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/swiftmandarin-learning-direction-checks"

# The opt-in flag leaves the external runner inert if Xcode ever sees it as an
# app source. It also compiles out `LearningContext.current`, the one accessor
# that reaches into app state, so the mirror logic can be checked on its own.
DEVELOPER_DIR="${DEVELOPER_DIR:-/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer}" \
    xcrun swiftc \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Models/LearningContext.swift" \
    "$repo_root/scripts/learning-direction-checks/LearningDirectionChecksRunner.swift" \
    -D LEARNING_DIRECTION_CHECKS \
    -swift-version 6 \
    -strict-concurrency=complete \
    -warnings-as-errors \
    -parse-as-library \
    -o "$binary_path"

"$binary_path"

# Reversal is only real if the app actually asks. These greps fail loudly when a
# surface that must mirror stops consulting the learning direction — the exact
# regression that leaves the reverse mode half-applied.
count_matches() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -o -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# The vocabulary list must size and order the row by the studied language, and
# must offer the English pronunciation where pinyin does not apply.
vocab_headword=$(count_matches 'renderedHeadwordFontSize' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/VocabularyView.swift")

#!/bin/zsh

set -euo pipefail

repo_root="${0:A:h:h}"
binary_path="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/swiftmandarin-learning-direction-checks"

# The opt-in flag leaves the external runner inert if Xcode ever sees it as an
# app source. It also compiles out `LearningContext.current`, the one accessor
# that reaches into app state, so the mirror logic can be checked on its own.
DEVELOPER_DIR="${DEVELOPER_DIR:-/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer}" \
    xcrun swiftc \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Models/LearningContext.swift" \
    "$repo_root/scripts/learning-direction-checks/LearningDirectionChecksRunner.swift" \
    -D LEARNING_DIRECTION_CHECKS \
    -swift-version 6 \
    -strict-concurrency=complete \
    -warnings-as-errors \
    -parse-as-library \
    -o "$binary_path"

"$binary_path"

# Reversal is only real if the app actually asks. These greps fail loudly when a
# surface that must mirror stops consulting the learning direction — the exact
# regression that leaves the reverse mode half-applied.
count_matches() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -o -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# The vocabulary list must size and order the row by the studied language, and
# must offer the English pronunciation where pinyin does not apply.
vocab_headword=$(count_matches 'renderedHeadwordFontSize' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/VocabularyView.swift")
vocab_phonetic=$(count_matches 'term\.showsPhonetic' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/VocabularyView.swift")
[[ "$vocab_headword" -ge 2 ]] || {
    print -u2 "The vocabulary row no longer sizes the headword by its language; found $vocab_headword"
    exit 1
}
[[ "$vocab_phonetic" -ge 3 ]] || {
    print -u2 "The vocabulary list/detail views no longer show an English pronunciation; found $vocab_phonetic"
    exit 1
}

# The tappable reader must follow the learner, not the content.
translate_reader=$(count_matches 'interactiveReaderIsChinese' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/TranslateView.swift")
translate_english_ruby=$(count_matches 'EnglishRubyTextView\(' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/TranslateView.swift")
[[ "$translate_reader" -ge 4 ]] || {
    print -u2 "Translate no longer picks its interactive pane by learning direction; found $translate_reader"
    exit 1
}
[[ "$translate_english_ruby" == "1" ]] || {
    print -u2 "Translate no longer offers the English word-by-word reader; found $translate_english_ruby"
    exit 1
}

# Pinyin ruby is scaffolding for a Mandarin learner only.
ruby_gate=$(count_matches 'showPinyin && localization\.learningIsChinese' "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/RubyTextView.swift")
[[ "$ruby_gate" == "1" ]] || {
    print -u2 "Pinyin ruby is no longer gated on the learning direction; found $ruby_gate"
    exit 1
}

# A first launch must open on the direction the learner mode implies.
persisted_default=$(count_matches 'TranslationDirection\.persistedDefault' \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/TranslateView.swift" \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/MoreView.swift" \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/MacOSSettingsView.swift" \
    "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Models/TranslationState.swift")
[[ "$persisted_default" == "4" ]] || {
    print -u2 "A reader of the default direction still hard-codes English→Chinese; found $persisted_default of 4"
    exit 1
}

print "Learning direction wiring checks passed (6/6)"

import json, xcstrings, re
adds = json.load(open('zh_batch2.json'))
cat = xcstrings.load()
s = cat['strings']

# Sanity: every %-placeholder in the key must be answerable by the translation.
spec = re.compile(r'%(?:(\d+)\$)?(lld|@|d|f|%)')
problems = []
for k, v in adds.items():
    ks = [m.group(2) for m in spec.finditer(k) if m.group(2) != '%']
    vs = [m.group(2) for m in spec.finditer(v) if m.group(2) != '%']
    if sorted(ks) != sorted(vs):
        problems.append((k, ks, vs))
for p in problems:
    print('PLACEHOLDER MISMATCH:', p)
assert not problems, 'fix placeholders before writing'

created = added = skipped = 0
for key, value in adds.items():
    entry = s.get(key)
    if entry is None:
        entry = {}
        s[key] = entry
        created += 1
    locs = entry.setdefault('localizations', {})
    if 'zh-Hans' in locs:
        skipped += 1
        continue
    locs['zh-Hans'] = {'stringUnit': {'state': 'translated', 'value': value}}
    added += 1

xcstrings.save(cat)
total = len(s)
have = sum(1 for v in s.values() if 'zh-Hans' in v.get('localizations', {}))
print(f'new-keys={created} translated={added} skipped={skipped}  coverage={have}/{total}')
EOF

# Handoff.md — SwiftMandarin: Bilingual + Multi-Provider AI Overhaul

**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-07-27
**Status:** In Progress (iter 28 — translation study notes, transcription repair, AI transcription; see Iteration 28)
**Prior Status:** In Progress (iter 27 — structured AI translation output; see Iteration 27)
**Prior Status:** In Progress (iter 16 — step-change overhaul on branch `jul-07-2026-step-change-overhaul`: RECOMMENDATIONS.md + Home dashboard + FSRS + Reader + AI conversation + UI overhaul)
**Current Focus (latest):** Photo-tab workbook expansion — direct camera capture, a review-question **database** (bank), AI **review-question generation**, **grading history** with the original scanned photos, **analytics** integration (graded questions in the contribution heatmap), and a decluttered **More** tab. Plus a 43-agent codebase audit written to `EXECPLAN2.md` (132 findings, 23 confirmed). See Updates iter 11.
**Prior Focus:** Interface-language-driven tailoring: when the UI is 中文 the user is treated as a native Mandarin speaker learning English (AI explanations written in Mandarin; saved words show ENGLISH as the big headline with Mandarin small; English TTS emphasis) and vice versa for English UI. Full audit + plan: docs/language-direction-audit.md (11-agent parallel map + completeness critic, 2026-06-13).
**Prior Focus:** Full-app audit + overhaul: 18 verified bug fixes, integration wins (unified history/stats, pinyin position, provider test connection), zero-warning builds, bilingual READMEs — see Updates iter 8 (2026-06-10).
**Prior Focus:** Full UI localization (English ⇄ 中文) with a runtime in-app language toggle — see Updates iter 5 (2026-06-07).
**Prior Focus:** Four-part overhaul — (A) fix photo OCR Chinese gibberish/language lock, (B) multi-provider cloud AI with API-fetched model lists, (C) photo→AI cleanup toggle, (D) make the app fully bilingual (dual narration + learner-mode toggle).

## 1) Request & Context
- **A — Photo OCR bug:** Photo upload "often produces gibberish," "cannot switch languages," "stuck on detecting English, can't read Mandarin."
- **B — Provider expansion:** Add OpenAI, Claude (Anthropic), Deepseek, Doubao, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu, Minimax. Pull each provider's available models via API.
- **C — Deep AI integration:** A settings toggle that routes an uploaded photo to an AI model for cleanup/structuring, returning cleaned text into the app.
- **D — Bilingual:** App must serve English-speakers-learning-Mandarin AND Mandarin-speakers-learning-English (and both). Add English narration alongside Mandarin for the selected word, and a settings toggle that flips the app between English-centric and Mandarin-centric, adapting features.

**Environment:** Xcode 26.3, iOS/macOS/visionOS **26.2** deploy targets, Swift 5 mode, single target `SwiftMandarin`, sandboxed (`ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX=YES`), generated Info.plist. One SPM dep: `ollama-swift 1.8.0`. State = `@Observable @MainActor` singletons over UserDefaults JSON. No Keychain, no network entitlement yet.

## 2) Verified Root Causes (from full-codebase read + 9-agent comprehension workflow)
**A (compounding 4-stage failure):**
1. `PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204` — `recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"]` English-first; `automaticallyDetectsLanguage` never set; no per-call override → genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. `:207` — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally → English autocorrect mangles Chinese into Latin gibberish.
3. `:45-72` (+ dup in `PhotoTranslateView:601`, `CameraScannerView:123`) — English-centric cleaner joins with spaces / English punctuation regex → corrupts spaceless Chinese.
4. `PhotoTranslateView:573-598` — language detection runs AFTER OCR on already-garbled text; non-Chinese falls back to English; `TextRecognitionResult.language` hardwired `nil`.
Secondary: `CameraScannerView:40` `.text()` no language hint; `VNImageRequestHandler` ignores orientation; `Character.isChineseCharacter` misses ranges.

**B:** `AIProvider` enum has only `.appleIntelligence`/`.ollama`; `AIModelSettings` Ollama-shaped, no API key storage; `OllamaService` (third-party `Ollama.Client`) can't reach cloud (hardcoded `/api/*`, no auth header). Exhaustive switches at `AIModelSettings:124,134`, `AIWordExplanationService:395,411`, `MacOSSettingsView:280`, `MoreView:471`; availability hardcoded in `ShortcutHelpers:95`, `AIWordExplanationView:27`.

**C:** Seam = `PhotoTranslateView.loadAndProcessImage` between `recognizeText(from:)` (`:508`) and `sourceText = result.cleanedText` (`:512`). No toggle, no image-capable provider today.

**D:** Narration single-language (`WordDetailPopover:272` Chinese only; `EnglishWordDetailSheet:184` English only). No learner-mode concept; defaults hardcoded English-first (`TranslationDirection`, `TranslationState`).

## 3) Plan & Decomposition
**Group 1 — Foundations:** entitlements network.client; `KeychainHelper`; `AppPreferences` (LearnerMode, PhotoScanLanguage, dualNarration); extend `AIProvider` + per-provider metadata + per-provider config/keys in `AIModelSettings` (generalized switches via `default:`); `CloudAIService` (URLSession; OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic; listModels w/ fallback; chat; vision; translate).
**Group 2 — OCR (A):** robust CJK-ratio-first detector + widened CJK in `ChineseTextAnalyzer`; parameterized recognition + Chinese-aware clean + language populated + orientation in `PhotoTextRecognitionService`; `.text(languages:)` in `CameraScannerView`; scan-language override UI + AI-cleanup hook + Chinese-aware processing in `PhotoTranslateView`.
**Group 3 — AI routing (B/C):** cloud dispatch + `cleanupRecognizedText` + tolerant JSON in `AIWordExplanationService`; cloud availability in `ShortcutHelpers`, `AIWordExplanationView`.
**Group 4 — Settings UI (B/C/D):** shared `AIProviderConfigView`; wire into `MacOSSettingsView` + `MoreView`; add learner-mode + photo-cleanup toggles.
**Group 5 — Narration (D):** dual narration in `WordDetailPopover` + `EnglishWordDetailSheet`.

## 4) Requirements → Acceptance Checks
| Req | Check | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A | Scan Chinese textbook → Chinese chars recognized, not gibberish; manual 中文/English/Auto switch works | macOS build + manual |
| B | Settings shows 10 providers; entering key + Refresh lists models from API | build + manual |
| C | Toggle ON → photo OCR text cleaned by AI before display | build + manual |
| D | Word detail shows both 朗读中文 + Read English; learner-mode toggle flips defaults | build + manual |
| All | `xcodebuild` macOS Debug succeeds, zero errors | pending |

## 5) Decisions
- Cloud clients via **URLSession** (no new SPM deps). All Chinese providers are OpenAI-compatible; Anthropic uses `/v1/messages` + `x-api-key`.
- API keys in **Keychain** (generic password), never UserDefaults.
- Exhaustive `AIProvider` switches converted to use `default:` (cloud) so future providers don't break compilation.
- `live model list` falls back to curated `defaultModels` per provider when the `/models` endpoint is absent/blocked.
- Learner mode adjusts defaults (direction, scan language) and is additive — never removes capability; dual narration always offered when both languages available.

## 6) Progress Ledger
- [x] G1 foundations — entitlements `network.client`; `KeychainHelper`; `AppPreferences`; extended `AIProvider` (10 providers) + per-provider keys/models in `AIModelSettings`; `CloudAIService` (URLSession, OpenAI + Anthropic, vision, model listing).
- [x] G2 OCR (A) — robust CJK-ratio detector + widened CJK in `ChineseTextAnalyzer`; parameterized recognition language + Chinese-aware cleaning + language carried + EXIF orientation in `PhotoTextRecognitionService`; `.text(languages:)` + language-aware cleaning in `CameraScannerView`; scan-language menu + "重新识别" + AI-cleanup hook + Chinese-aware processing in `PhotoTranslateView`.
